<header>
<div class="eyebrow">Python module · Standard library only</div>
<h1>Password hashing in Python</h1>
<p class="muted">Constant-time string comparison, salted PBKDF2 password hashing, and verification, with the complete unit test suite in one downloadable Python file.</p>
<div class="actions"><a class="button" download="secure_passwords.py" href="data:text/plain;charset=utf-8;base64,">Download secure_passwords.py</a><a class="button secondary" href="#implementation">View source &amp; tests</a></div>
</header>
<div class="stats" aria-label="Hashing parameters">
<div class="stat"><strong>600,000</strong><span>Default PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 iterations</span></div>
<div class="stat"><strong>16 bytes</strong><span>Fresh cryptographically random salt</span></div>
<div class="stat"><strong>32 bytes</strong><span>Derived key, compared with compare_digest</span></div>
</div>
<section aria-labelledby="usage-title">
<h2 id="usage-title">Use the module</h2>
<p>Download the Python file, or copy the complete source below into <code>secure_passwords.py</code>. Requires Python 3.10 or later with OpenSSL support. No packages to install. The HTML and download work offline.</p>
<pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Python usage example"><code>from secure_passwords import constant_time_compare, hash_password, verify

assert constant_time_compare("same", "same")
assert not constant_time_compare("same", "different")

stored = hash_password("correct horse battery staple")
assert verify("correct horse battery staple", stored)
assert not verify("wrong password", stored)

# Save the entire 'stored' string; it contains the salt and work factor.</code></pre>
<p>Execute all included unit tests:</p>
<pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Test command"><code>python3 secure_passwords.py -v</code></pre>
</section>
<section aria-labelledby="contract-title">
<h2 id="contract-title">API and record format</h2>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Function</th><th scope="col">Behavior</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td><code>constant_time_compare(left, right)</code></td><td>Accepts two strings, encodes them as UTF-8 and compares the bytes using <code>hmac.compare_digest</code>. Returns a Boolean.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>hash_password(password, *, iterations=600_000)</code></td><td>Generates a new random salt with <code>secrets.token_bytes</code> on every call. Returns a versioned record. Accepts integer work factors from 600,000 through 5,000,000; Boolean values are rejected.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>verify(password, encoded_hash)</code></td><td>Returns <code>True</code> only for a matching password and supported record. Malformed records, unsupported versions, invalid password values, and work factors outside the accepted range return <code>False</code> before derivation. Wrong argument types raise <code>TypeError</code>.</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>
<pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Stored record format"><code>pbkdf2_sha256$1$iterations$salt_hex$derived_key_hex
             ↑            ↑        ↑
          version     32 hex    64 hex
                     characters characters</code></pre>
<p>Passwords are strings of at most 1,024 UTF-8 bytes. They are never truncated or normalized. Empty strings and embedded NUL characters are supported. Hashing invalid values raises <code>ValueError</code>; non-string inputs raise <code>TypeError</code>. The comparison helper rejects unpaired Unicode surrogates with <code>UnicodeEncodeError</code>. Unexpected random-source or hashing failures propagate.</p>
</section>
<aside class="note" aria-label="Timing guarantees">
<p><strong>What constant time means here.</strong> The comparison primitive avoids early exits based on matching content. String encoding and input lengths may still affect runtime. Verification compares two fixed-size derived keys, but parsing errors and different work factors take different amounts of time. Unit tests check behavior and use of the primitive; they do not prove timing guarantees. See <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/hmac.html#hmac.compare_digest">Python’s compare_digest documentation</a>.</p>
</aside>
<p class="muted">The default follows <a href="https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Password_Storage_Cheat_Sheet.html#pbkdf2">OWASP’s PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 guidance</a>. The module uses <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/hashlib.html#hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac">Python’s PBKDF2 implementation</a>. Benchmark the work factor for your service; this module accepts only the documented record version and iteration range.</p>
<section id="implementation" aria-labelledby="source-title">
<div class="code-bar"><h2 id="source-title">Complete source &amp; unit tests</h2><div class="copy-controls"><button class="button secondary" id="copy" type="button">Copy Python source</button></div></div>
<div id="copy-status" role="status" aria-live="polite"></div>
<pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Complete Python module"><code id="python-source">&quot;&quot;&quot;Standard-library password hashing. Python 3.10+ with OpenSSL required.

Run tests: python3 secure_passwords.py -v
Record: pbkdf2_sha256$1$&lt;iterations&gt;$&lt;salt hex&gt;$&lt;derived key hex&gt;
Passwords use strict UTF-8, without normalization or truncation. Empty
passwords are supported; enforce password policy in the application.
Only the content comparison avoids early mismatch exits. Encoding, lengths,
parsing and variable work factors can affect total verification time.
&quot;&quot;&quot;

import hashlib
import hmac
import re
import secrets
import unittest
from unittest import mock

__all__ = [&quot;constant_time_compare&quot;, &quot;hash_password&quot;, &quot;verify&quot;]
MIN_ITERATIONS = 600_000
DEFAULT_ITERATIONS = 600_000
MAX_ITERATIONS = 5_000_000
SALT_BYTES = 16
KEY_BYTES = 32
MAX_PASSWORD_BYTES = 1024
MAX_RECORD_CHARS = 128
_RECORD = re.compile(
    r&quot;pbkdf2_sha256\$1\$([1-9][0-9]{0,6})\$&quot;
    r&quot;([0-9a-f]{32})\$([0-9a-f]{64})&quot;
)


def _require_string(value: str, name: str) -&gt; None:
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        raise TypeError(f&quot;{name} must be a str&quot;)


def _password_bytes(password: ***REDACTED*** -&gt; bytes:
    _require_string(password, &quot;password&quot;)
    # Bound allocation before encoding, then check the actual byte length.
    if len(password) &gt; MAX_PASSWORD_BYTES:
        raise ValueError(&quot;password exceeds 1024 UTF-8 bytes&quot;)
    try:
        encoded = password.encode(&quot;utf-8&quot;)
    except UnicodeEncodeError:
        raise ValueError(&quot;password must contain valid UTF-8 text&quot;) from None
    if len(encoded) &gt; MAX_PASSWORD_BYTES:
        raise ValueError(&quot;password exceeds 1024 UTF-8 bytes&quot;)
    return encoded


def constant_time_compare(left: str, right: str) -&gt; bool:
    &quot;&quot;&quot;Compare UTF-8 strings using hmac.compare_digest.

    Avoids content-dependent early exits; lengths and encoding costs can
    remain observable. No Unicode normalization is performed. Non-strings
    raise TypeError; unpaired surrogates raise UnicodeEncodeError.
    &quot;&quot;&quot;
    _require_string(left, &quot;left&quot;)
    _require_string(right, &quot;right&quot;)
    return hmac.compare_digest(left.encode(&quot;utf-8&quot;), right.encode(&quot;utf-8&quot;))


def hash_password(password: ***REDACTED***, *, iterations: int = DEFAULT_ITERATIONS) -&gt; str:
    &quot;&quot;&quot;Return a PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 record with a fresh random 16-byte salt.

    Store the entire record. Salt and iteration count are public.
    Iterations must be an int (not bool) in [600_000, 5_000_000].
    Wrong types raise TypeError; invalid values raise ValueError.
    &quot;&quot;&quot;
    password_bytes = _password_bytes(password)
    if type(iterations) is not int:
        raise TypeError(&quot;iterations must be an int&quot;)
    if not MIN_ITERATIONS &lt;= iterations &lt;= MAX_ITERATIONS:
        raise ValueError(&quot;iterations must be between 600000 and 5000000&quot;)
    salt = secrets.token_bytes(SALT_BYTES)
    key = hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac(
        &quot;sha256&quot;, password_bytes, salt, iterations, dklen=KEY_BYTES
    )
    return f&quot;pbkdf2_sha256$1${iterations}${salt.hex()}${key.hex()}&quot;


def verify(password: ***REDACTED***, encoded_hash: str) -&gt; bool:
    &quot;&quot;&quot;Verify a complete record produced by hash_password.

    Return False for a mismatch, malformed/unsupported record, out-of-range
    work factor, or invalid password value. Non-string arguments raise
    TypeError. Unexpected runtime errors propagate. Validate record bounds
    before derivation; compare the resulting fixed-size keys securely.
    &quot;&quot;&quot;
    _require_string(password, &quot;password&quot;)
    _require_string(encoded_hash, &quot;encoded_hash&quot;)
    if len(encoded_hash) &gt; MAX_RECORD_CHARS:
        return False
    match = _RECORD.fullmatch(encoded_hash)
    if match is None:
        return False
    rounds_text, salt_hex, key_hex = match.groups()
    iterations = int(rounds_text)
    if not MIN_ITERATIONS &lt;= iterations &lt;= MAX_ITERATIONS:
        return False
    try:
        password_bytes = _password_bytes(password)
    except ValueError:
        return False
    salt = bytes.fromhex(salt_hex)
    expected = bytes.fromhex(key_hex)
    actual = hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac(
        &quot;sha256&quot;, password_bytes, salt, iterations, dklen=KEY_BYTES
    )
    return hmac.compare_digest(actual, expected)


class ComparisonTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_equal_strings(self):
        for value in (&quot;&quot;, &quot;secret&quot;, &quot;a\x00b&quot;, &quot;密碼🔐&quot;):
            with self.subTest(value=value):
                self.assertTrue(constant_time_compare(value, value))

    def test_mismatches_and_lengths(self):
        for a, b in ((&quot;secret&quot;, &quot;xecret&quot;), (&quot;secret&quot;, &quot;secrex&quot;),
                     (&quot;secret&quot;, &quot;secrets&quot;), (&quot;&quot;, &quot;a&quot;), (&quot;a&quot;, &quot;&quot;)):
            with self.subTest(a=a, b=b):
                self.assertFalse(constant_time_compare(a, b))

    def test_no_unicode_normalization(self):
        self.assertFalse(constant_time_compare(&quot;é&quot;, &quot;e\u0301&quot;))

    def test_invalid_types(self):
        for value in (None, 42, b&quot;secret&quot;, bytearray(b&quot;secret&quot;)):
            with self.subTest(value=value):
                with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
                    constant_time_compare(value, &quot;secret&quot;)
                with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
                    constant_time_compare(&quot;secret&quot;, value)

    def test_invalid_unicode(self):
        with self.assertRaises(UnicodeEncodeError):
            constant_time_compare(&quot;\ud800&quot;, &quot;\ud800&quot;)

    def test_secure_comparison_primitive(self):
        # Functional delegation check, not a timing benchmark.
        with mock.patch.object(hmac, &quot;compare_digest&quot;,
                               wraps=hmac.compare_digest) as compare:
            self.assertTrue(constant_time_compare(&quot;密碼&quot;, &quot;密碼&quot;))
        compare.assert_called_once_with(&quot;密碼&quot;.encode(), &quot;密碼&quot;.encode())


class PasswordTests(unittest.TestCase):
    # Cross-checked with an independent PBKDF2 implementation:
    # U1 = HMAC(P, salt || INT32_BE(1)); Ui = HMAC(P, Ui-1); XOR all Ui.
    FIXTURE = (
        &quot;pbkdf2_sha256$1$600000$000102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f$&quot;
        &quot;3bc37118e625093e9b79ed08930ea7af7389591233fdd92dddf369371e60dbc0&quot;
    )

    def test_known_answer(self):
        with mock.patch.object(secrets, &quot;token_bytes&quot;,
                               return_value=bytes(range(16))):
            self.assertEqual(hash_password(&quot;password&quot;), self.FIXTURE)
        self.assertTrue(verify(&quot;password&quot;, self.FIXTURE))

    def test_round_trip_and_wrong_password(self):
        record = hash_password(&quot;correct horse battery staple&quot;)
        self.assertTrue(verify(&quot;correct horse battery staple&quot;, record))
        self.assertFalse(verify(&quot;incorrect horse battery staple&quot;, record))

    def test_format(self):
        algorithm, version, rounds, salt, key = hash_password(&quot;p&quot;).split(&quot;$&quot;)
        self.assertEqual((algorithm, version, rounds),
                         (&quot;pbkdf2_sha256&quot;, &quot;1&quot;, &quot;600000&quot;))
        self.assertEqual(len(bytes.fromhex(salt)), 16)
        self.assertEqual(len(bytes.fromhex(key)), 32)

    def test_random_salts(self):
        first, second = hash_password(&quot;same&quot;), hash_password(&quot;same&quot;)
        self.assertNotEqual(first.split(&quot;$&quot;)[3], second.split(&quot;$&quot;)[3])
        self.assertNotEqual(first, second)
        self.assertTrue(verify(&quot;same&quot;, first))
        self.assertTrue(verify(&quot;same&quot;, second))

    def test_fresh_secure_randomness_per_call(self):
        with mock.patch.object(secrets, &quot;token_bytes&quot;,
                               side_effect=[b&quot;a&quot; * 16, b&quot;b&quot; * 16]) as rng:
            first, second = hash_password(&quot;same&quot;), hash_password(&quot;same&quot;)
        self.assertEqual(rng.call_args_list, [mock.call(16), mock.call(16)])
        self.assertEqual(first.split(&quot;$&quot;)[3], (b&quot;a&quot; * 16).hex())
        self.assertEqual(second.split(&quot;$&quot;)[3], (b&quot;b&quot; * 16).hex())

    def test_empty_password(self):
        record = hash_password(&quot;&quot;)
        self.assertTrue(verify(&quot;&quot;, record))
        self.assertFalse(verify(&quot;nonempty&quot;, record))

    def test_unicode_password(self):
        record = hash_password(&quot;café 密碼🔐&quot;)
        self.assertTrue(verify(&quot;café 密碼🔐&quot;, record))
        self.assertFalse(verify(&quot;cafe\u0301 密碼🔐&quot;, record))

    def test_embedded_nul(self):
        record = hash_password(&quot;pass\x00word&quot;)
        self.assertTrue(verify(&quot;pass\x00word&quot;, record))
        self.assertFalse(verify(&quot;pass&quot;, record))
        self.assertFalse(verify(&quot;password&quot;, record))

    def test_maximum_password_length(self):
        for password in (&quot;a&quot; * 1024, &quot;🔐&quot; * 256):
            with self.subTest(characters=len(password)):
                record = hash_password(password)
                self.assertTrue(verify(password, record))
                self.assertFalse(verify(password[:-1], record))

    def test_invalid_password_values_skip_derivation(self):
        for password in (&quot;a&quot; * 1025, &quot;🔐&quot; * 257, &quot;\ud800&quot;):
            with self.subTest(characters=len(password)):
                with mock.patch.object(hashlib, &quot;pbkdf2_hmac&quot;) as derive:
                    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                        hash_password(password)
                    self.assertFalse(verify(password, self.FIXTURE))
                    derive.assert_not_called()

    def test_invalid_argument_types(self):
        for value in (None, 123, b&quot;password&quot;, False):
            with self.subTest(value=value):
                with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
                    hash_password(value)
                with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
                    verify(value, self.FIXTURE)
                with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
                    verify(&quot;password&quot;, value)

    def test_invalid_iterations(self):
        for rounds in (0, -1, 599_999, 5_000_001):
            with self.subTest(rounds=rounds):
                with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                    hash_password(&quot;p&quot;, iterations=rounds)
        for rounds in (True, False, 600_000.0, &quot;600000&quot;, None):
            with self.subTest(rounds=rounds):
                with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
                    hash_password(&quot;p&quot;, iterations=rounds)

    def test_stored_work_factor(self):
        record = hash_password(&quot;password&quot;, iterations=600_001)
        self.assertEqual(record.split(&quot;$&quot;)[2], &quot;600001&quot;)
        self.assertTrue(verify(&quot;password&quot;, record))
        self.assertFalse(verify(&quot;password&quot;,
                               record.replace(&quot;$600001$&quot;, &quot;$600000$&quot;)))

    def test_maximum_work_factor(self):
        record = hash_password(&quot;password&quot;, iterations=MAX_ITERATIONS)
        self.assertTrue(verify(&quot;password&quot;, record))

    def test_malformed_records_skip_derivation(self):
        malformed = [
            &quot;&quot;, &quot;garbage&quot;, self.FIXTURE + &quot;$extra&quot;, self.FIXTURE + &quot;\n&quot;,
            &quot; &quot; + self.FIXTURE, self.FIXTURE[:-1], self.FIXTURE.upper(),
            self.FIXTURE.replace(&quot;sha256&quot;, &quot;sha1&quot;),
            self.FIXTURE.replace(&quot;$1$&quot;, &quot;$2$&quot;, 1),
            self.FIXTURE.replace(&quot;00010203&quot;, &quot;gg010203&quot;, 1),
            self.FIXTURE.replace(&quot;00010203&quot;, &quot;0001 203&quot;, 1),
            self.FIXTURE.replace(&quot;00010203&quot;, &quot;000102&quot;, 1),
            self.FIXTURE[:-1] + &quot;g&quot;, self.FIXTURE[:-1] + &quot;\ud800&quot;,
            self.FIXTURE.split(&quot;$&quot;)[-1], &quot;x&quot; * 100_000,
        ]
        malformed.extend(
            self.FIXTURE.replace(&quot;$600000$&quot;, f&quot;${rounds}$&quot;)
            for rounds in (&quot;0&quot;, &quot;-1&quot;, &quot;+600000&quot;, &quot;0600000&quot;, &quot;599999&quot;,
                           &quot;5000001&quot;, &quot;99999999999999999999&quot;, &quot;600000.0&quot;,
                           &quot;６０００００&quot;, &quot;&quot;, &quot;600 000&quot;)
        )
        with mock.patch.object(hashlib, &quot;pbkdf2_hmac&quot;) as derive:
            for record in malformed:
                with self.subTest(record=record[:140]):
                    self.assertFalse(verify(&quot;password&quot;, record))
            derive.assert_not_called()

    def test_modified_salt_or_key(self):
        parts = self.FIXTURE.split(&quot;$&quot;)
        for index in (3, 4):
            altered = parts.copy()
            first = &quot;0&quot; if parts[index][0] != &quot;0&quot; else &quot;1&quot;
            altered[index] = first + parts[index][1:]
            with self.subTest(field=index):
                self.assertFalse(verify(&quot;password&quot;, &quot;$&quot;.join(altered)))

    def test_verification_compares_fixed_size_bytes(self):
        with mock.patch.object(hmac, &quot;compare_digest&quot;,
                               wraps=hmac.compare_digest) as compare:
            self.assertTrue(verify(&quot;password&quot;, self.FIXTURE))
        compare.assert_called_once()
        actual, expected = compare.call_args.args
        self.assertIsInstance(actual, bytes)
        self.assertIsInstance(expected, bytes)
        self.assertEqual((len(actual), len(expected)), (32, 32))

    def test_runtime_failures_propagate(self):
        with mock.patch.object(secrets, &quot;token_bytes&quot;,
                               side_effect=OSError(&quot;RNG failed&quot;)):
            with self.assertRaises(OSError):
                hash_password(&quot;password&quot;)
        with mock.patch.object(hashlib, &quot;pbkdf2_hmac&quot;,
                               side_effect=RuntimeError(&quot;KDF failed&quot;)):
            with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError):
                verify(&quot;password&quot;, self.FIXTURE)


if __name__ == &quot;__main__&quot;:
    unittest.main()
</code></pre>

<script>
const copyButton = document.getElementById('copy');
copyButton.addEventListener('click', async () => {
  const source = document.getElementById('python-source');
  const status = document.getElementById('copy-status');
  try {
    await navigator.clipboard.writeText(source.textContent);
    status.textContent = 'Python source and tests copied.';
  } catch (error) {
    const range = document.createRange();
    range.selectNodeContents(source);
    const selection = window.getSelection();
    selection.removeAllRanges();
    selection.addRange(range);
    status.textContent = 'Source selected. Press Ctrl+C or Command+C to copy.';
  }
});
</script>
